Born in Columbia Heights, Minnesota, Bakken had a long-held fascination with electricity and electronics. In the cell as developed for cardiac pacemaker application, the anode is lithium and the cathode a proprietary

"Rune Elmqvist"
Rune Elmqvist Rune Elmqvist (1906–1996) developed the first implantable pacemaker in 1958, working under the direction of Åke Senning, senior physician and cardiac surgeon at the Karolinska University Hospital in Solna, Sweden. Elmqvist initially worked as a medical doctor (having trained in Lund), but later worked as an engineer and inventor.
